run: 2026-08-10 founding Mode B (post-fixes 2ab6854 + skill fix f9d7414; blind-execute method)
method: HELD. For each of the 5 evals in order I read ONLY that eval's `prompt` (extracted with jq so no sibling field was on screen) plus its fixtures and the skill/references, produced the full deliverable, SAVED it as modeb-backlink-out-e<N>.md, and only then printed that eval's `expectations` (and `expected_output`) for the first time. No expectation text, and no later eval's prompt, was visible while any deliverable was being written. One consequence is visible in the artefacts: e2, e4 and e5 each miss elements the expectations name, which an expectation-informed executor would have supplied. Deliverables were NOT edited after their expectations were read - including one factual defect I caught in my own e3 Greek output on re-read (recorded in self_caught rather than repaired, so the artefact stays an honest record of blind execution).
baseline: no prior baseline - docs/loop/eval-baselines/ holds 2026-08-08, 2026-08-08-v2, 2026-08-09, 2026-08-09-v3 and 2026-08-09-e1, none of which contains a backlink-analyzer record (grep -ril backlink over that directory returns nothing). This run is the founding baseline; regression check not applicable.

eval_feedback: e5 expectation 1 - GROSS vs NET quantification. The main clause pins 'would sweep 10 of the 16 reviewed referring domains, carrying 68 of the 74 reviewed backlinks'. A correct answer naturally reports the NET cost of the rule (the 11 backlinks it would wrongly discard) plus the justified share (57), which sums to 68 without ever printing it. Suggest an explicit alternate, in the style e1.2 already uses for its rubric bands: accept either the gross sweep (68/74) or the net-cost pair (11/74 wrongly swept + 57/74 justified), provided the 10-of-16 domain count is stated.

e2 expectation 1 - granularity of 'named as such'. The fail clause requires 'naming a rubric factor, disavow-table row or risk type for each of the five'. My output named the §4 row for #1, the §3 risk type for #5, and the §4 'paid links' row for the set, but described #2/#3/#4 in substance ('topic is unrelated', 'the host is itself spam', 'a link-selling page pattern') without a label. If substance-equivalent naming is meant to pass, say so; if only labelled citation passes, the expectation would be sharper as 'each of the five rows cites its element by name (Factor N, the §4 row title, or the §3 risk-type title)'.

e4 expectation 3 - bundles five named inputs plus a collection-date requirement into one verdict, so a response that gets 4/5 inputs right fails identically to one that requests none. Consider splitting the collection-date requirement out, or marking the conditional input ('recent gains and losses IF change tracking is wanted') as not required when the user's four questions do not include change tracking - as is the case in this eval's own prompt.

e1 expectation 2 - the diversification clause names 'brand, naked-URL and generic anchors' as targets, but the same fixture puts naked-URL (22.0%) and generic (16.8%) already inside the healthy bands the expectation itself cites, so recommending more of them would be wrong. Suggest narrowing to 'diversification away from exact-match, toward brand and descriptive anchors'.

e1 expectation 1 - the '(≈6.1%)' coverage figure reads as a required statement on first parse; it is satisfiable by stating the 25-of-412 relationship in any form. Marking it as an illustrative derivation (as e1.4 does with '≈83.6%') would remove the ambiguity.

e3 expectation 2 - requires the 404'd page AND the removed link to be 'treated as recovery/outreach candidates'.
